simple.meaning: דָּלַל (dâlal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to slacken or be feeble ; figuratively, to be oppressed.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 9 times in Judges, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, beginning at Judges 6:6. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּלַל (H1809) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דָּלַל (dâlal) / H1809 is traced through Judges 6:6, Job 28:4, Psalms 79:8, Psalms 116:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to slacken or be feeble ; figuratively, to be oppressed
definitions.usage: bring low, dry up, be emptied, be not equal, fail, be impoverished, be made thin.
definitions.full: H1809. dalal דָּלַל verb hang, be low, languish (Late Hebrew Hiph`il thin, thin out vines, etc.; Assyrian dalâlu , be weak , humble Zim Bp 74. 97 ; Arabic direct, guide , , be directed, guided ; put in motion, commotion ; be in motion, hang, dangle ; also amorous, coquettish, gesture or behaviour of women) — Qal Perfect דֵּלֹּתִי Psa 116:6 , דַּלּוֺתִי 142:7 ; 1 plural דַּלּוֺנוּ 79:8 , דָּֽלֲלוּ Isa 19:6 , דַּלּוּ 38:14 ; Job 28:4 (on דַּלְיוּ Prov 26:7 compare דָּלָה ); — hang, 'depend' , Job 28:4 (of one descending a miner's shaft || נָעוּ ); be low , of streams Isa 19:6 (|| חָֽרְבוּ ); be low, brought low , metaphor of distress Psa 79:8 ; 116:6 ; 142:7 ; languish , of eyes, look languishingly (Che) Isa 38:14 . — Niph`al Imperfect יִדַּל Isa 17:4 , וַיִּדַּל Judg 6:6 , — be brought low, laid low , 6:6 figurative of Israel; Isa 17:4 of glory of Jacob.

occurrences.englishText: Israel was brought very low because of Midian; and the children of Israel cried to Yahweh.
He breaks open a shaft away from where people live.
Don’t hold the iniquities of our forefathers against us.
Bring my soul out of prison,
Like the legs of the lame that hang loose,
“It will happen in that day that the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.
The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.
I chattered like a swallow or a crane.
